title: Tabro MCP contract version 5
description: Eighteen tools: thirteen durable asynchronous operations, four reads and terminal request closure. Extension-registered Profiles have broker/user launch ownership; lifecycle tickets retain authenticated requester authority. Pairing aliases are the sole public Profile names.

broker_issued_ref.description: An opaque reference issued by the broker and echoed unchanged by the agent.

broker_issued_cursor.description: An opaque pagination or event cursor issued by the broker and echoed unchanged by the agent.

request_ref.description: A request-ticket reference issued by the broker after durable acceptance.

window_ref.description: A logical browser-window reference issued by the broker.

endpoint_nickname.description: A human-readable nickname generated by one profile-local extension during pairing and unique in the local broker registry.

workspace_ownership_frozen.description: True while an accepted kill_browser_endpoint or resume_browser_endpoint ticket for this endpoint is nonterminal. Existing active workspace ownership cannot change until that ticket terminates.

ownership.description: Browser launch ownership. Broker can reopen the Profile through MCP; user opens Chrome manually. Both support workspace automation while connected.

window_fact.description: A broker-observed browser window. Eligibility and recency are facts used by workspace selection; they are not Chrome window IDs.

ownership.description: Browser launch ownership. Broker can reopen the Profile through MCP; user opens Chrome manually. Both support workspace automation while connected.

capability_fact.description: One current extension-backed managed-tab CDP capability observation.

automation_pause_reasons.description: Independent active workspace control causes. The list can contain both endpoint_killed and manual_workspace_stop.

workspace_request_summary_fact.description: One bounded current-owner-visible workspace-operation summary used to discover a broker-issued request_ref before reading the full ticket. Requester-scoped acquisition and takeover-control tickets and endpoint-wide tickets are excluded.

oneOf.description: A page of request references visible under the current workspace-owner epoch. This view lets a replacement owner discover active tickets transferred by takeover.

request_browser_workspace_input.description: required_workspace_count counts distinct endpoints. The caller input may repeat a designated endpoint nickname; the broker normalizes exact repeats so each counts once, and the accepted ticket's normalized designated set is distinct and cannot exceed the count. Omitting window_ref requests the most-recently-focused eligible existing window on that endpoint. If several eligible windows exist without focus history, execution fails with WINDOW_UNAVAILABLE and the agent retries with a broker-issued window_ref. Different window_ref values on repeated entries reject synchronously as INVALID_ARGUMENT.

workspace_request_facts.description: resolved contains exactly requested_workspace_count entries with distinct endpoint nicknames. Insufficient eligible endpoint capacity is rejected before ticket issuance.

workspace_request_failure_facts.description: Known workspace side effects if accepted acquisition later fails; this is not a partial-success result.

command_restart_replacement_facts.description: The original raw command's failed terminal facts after replacement creation succeeds.

command_restart_exhaustion_facts.description: The shared terminal facts after all three restart_failed replacement attempts are exhausted. The original raw command and winning resolver are failed, queued old-tab followers are failed without dispatch or retargeting, the old tab remains managed, and the lane is released atomically.

invalidated_tab_request_replacement_fact.description: Exact facts for a queued old-tab command invalidated without dispatch or retargeting after restart_failed successfully creates a replacement tab.

invalidated_tab_request_exhaustion_facts.description: Exact facts for a queued old-tab command invalidated without dispatch or retargeting after all three restart_failed replacement attempts exhaust.

invalidated_tab_request_failure_facts.description: The exact queued-follower facts. A non-null replacement_tab selects successful replacement; null selects total replacement exhaustion.

ticket_access_transferred.description: Every still-public owner-governed workspace-operation ticket moved to the new owner. Requester-scoped acquisition and takeover-control tickets are excluded.

termination_facts.description: Successful termination facts are returned only after all dispatched work reconciles and the archive-suffixed tab-group rename is confirmed.

ticket_inspection_preserved.description: The terminating owner keeps ticket-only read and close authority for still-public owner-governed operation tickets until their approved terminal results and closure.

workspace_requests_cursor_reset.description: Pre-termination request-discovery cursors are invalid; a fresh query is required under ended-workspace ticket authority.

termination_failure_facts.description: Known facts when termination cannot complete required reconciliation and archive confirmation. The ticket is failed, agent control remains active, and the workspace remains paused for explicit recovery.

request_resolution_facts.description: The succeeded result of the single broker-side target-resolution compare-and-write winner. A restart_failed winner whose three replacement attempts exhaust instead uses a failed ticket with command_restart_exhaustion_facts. A competing resolver must not mutate the browser, terminalize the target, or release its lane and ends failed, never uncertain, with REQUEST_RESOLUTION_RACE_LOST.

workspace_resume_facts.description: A reconciled workspace after clearing only manual_workspace_stop. endpoint_killed can remain independently active. Resume does not replay a browser request.

endpoint_kill_facts.description: Returned only after admission proves that the caller owns every active workspace on the endpoint. The nonterminal ownership freeze has ended by terminal success.

endpoint_resume_facts.description: Returned only after admission proves that the caller owns every active workspace on the endpoint. The nonterminal ownership freeze has ended by terminal success.

request_checkpoint.description: A durable implementation-neutral diagnostic checkpoint. Phase and checkpoint names are nonempty implementation-defined strings; lifecycle, pause condition, problem, and available actions remain the control vocabulary.

async_request_body.description: The exact normalized body constructed by the broker from one accepted asynchronous tool invocation. It never contains an agent-created identifier.

request_resolution_exhaustion_failure.description: The exact failed winning-resolver payload after all three restart_failed replacement attempts exhaust. It reuses the existing human_resolution_restart_failed failure kind and selects no public problem code.

invalidated_tab_request_failure.description: The dedicated failure envelope for a queued old-tab command invalidated by restart_failed. The failure kind is public and structurally selects exact follower facts, while problem remains null so this proposal does not choose the still-open public problem code.

request_uncertainty.description: A terminal uncertainty for tools whose non-race domain effect remains allowed to end uncertain. create_browser_tab, send_cdp_command, and terminate_workspace are deliberately excluded. Losing takeover, termination, and resolution races are also failed, never uncertain.

request_ticket.description: The authority-visible ticket. Workspace-acquisition, takeover-control, and endpoint-control tickets remain requester-scoped through terminal closure. Ordinary workspace-operation tickets follow current workspace-owner authority. A winning takeover atomically transfers every still-public owner-governed operation ticket to the replacement owner; requester-scoped tickets do not transfer. Endpoint kill and resume require complete endpoint ownership at admission and freeze existing active workspace ownership until the accepted control ticket terminates; takeover rejects synchronously during that freeze. Lifecycle state and nullable pause_condition are separate. A nonterminal same-tab head retains its broker-private lane through pause and reconciliation; direct polling does not affect lane release. Terminal states are monotonic. Losing control races are failed, never uncertain. Tool discriminators in result, failure, or uncertainty equal request.tool.

request_submission_output.description: Accepted means durable admission, not execution success. The ticket response must be delivered before dispatch; delivery failure means no dispatch and is an immediate transport bug. Rejected submissions contain no ticket or request_ref. No asynchronous input carries an agent deadline, no public tool cancels one ticket, and the broker applies no elapsed-time terminal timeout.

get_browser_request_output.description: Only the applicable authority may read the ticket. Workspace acquisition uses its requesting prospective-owner authority; takeover-control uses its replacement requester; and endpoint-control uses its accepting requester through terminal closure. Ordinary workspace-operation tickets use current workspace-owner authority. An authorized subagent call may act under owner authority but gains no independent entitlement. At a winning takeover commit, every still-public owner-governed operation ticket moves to the new owner and the former owner loses access; requester-scoped tickets do not transfer. Previously unknown transferred operation request_ref values are discoverable through the paginated workspace_requests context view, which excludes acquisition, takeover-control, and endpoint-wide tickets. Takeover rejects synchronously during a nonterminal endpoint ownership freeze. The broker enforces that any polling action's request_ref equals the returned ticket request_ref.

close_browser_request_output.description: The applicable requester or current owner can close an already-terminal ticket. Acquisition, takeover-control, and endpoint-control requesters retain closure authority for their own tickets through terminal closure; ordinary workspace tickets require current-owner or ended-workspace ticket authority. Terminal/public state, applicable authority, and the current ticket or owner epoch are compared in one atomic mutation, so stale authority cannot close after takeover. An authorized subagent call may act under owner authority but gains no independent entitlement. There is no automatic visibility timeout.

request_browser_workspace_output.description: On acceptance, the requesting session has prospective workspace-owner authority over this ticket before workspace realization and retains that authority for every workspace the request creates.

terminate_workspace_output.description: After acceptance, termination fences new work and fails accepted browser work that has not started. It succeeds only after dispatched work reconciles and the archive rename is confirmed. Otherwise it ends failed with the workspace active and paused.

resume_workspace_automation_output.description: On success, reconciliation is complete and only manual_workspace_stop is cleared; endpoint_killed remains independently active when present.

kill_browser_endpoint_output.description: Synchronously rejected without a ticket unless the caller owns every active workspace on the endpoint. Rejection offers stop_workspace_automation actions for caller-owned workspaces that Tabro can identify. Acceptance freezes existing active workspace ownership until the ticket terminates. Takeover rejects synchronously during that freeze, and the accepting requester retains ticket read and close authority through terminal closure.

resume_browser_endpoint_output.description: Synchronously rejected without a ticket unless the caller owns every active workspace on the endpoint. Rejection offers stop_workspace_automation actions for caller-owned workspaces that Tabro can identify. Acceptance freezes existing active workspace ownership until the ticket terminates. Takeover rejects synchronously during that freeze, and the accepting requester retains ticket read and close authority through terminal closure.

profile_ref.description: Opaque persistent Profile reference issued by the Broker.

ownership.description: Browser launch ownership. Broker can reopen the Profile through MCP; user opens Chrome manually. Both support workspace automation while connected.
